requirements: R1: Add new Telegram accounts via OTP verification codes in the UI, or by uploading pre-authenticated .session / tdata files.
R2: Mandatory assignment of dedicated IPv4/IPv6 proxies (SOCKS5/HTTP) per account.
R3: Real-time tracking of account status (Active, Spam-Block, Ban, Re-auth).
R4: Anti-fraud module enforcing randomized pauses and 'typing...' chat status signals.
R5: Strict limits on new outbound conversations per account per day to avoid flood controls.

slices.title: Telegram Account and Proxy Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing the core data layer for this epic, I want to define the PostgreSQL schema and JPA entities for TG_Accounts, Proxies, and Rate Limits, so that session status and configuration can be reliably persisted.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an empty database, When the Flyway migration runs, Then TG_Accounts and Proxy tables are created with proper foreign keys.
Given a new TG_Account entity, When persisted, Then it successfully stores proxy details and daily rate limits.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Database I/O for tracking session states
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 0% schema deployment failures during initial migration

slices.title: Shared API Contract for Session Management
slices.jtbd: When implementing the frontend-backend communication for this epic, I want to define the REST endpoints and DTOs for account onboarding and status tracking, so that both teams can build in parallel.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the OpenAPI specification, When generated, Then it includes endpoints for OTP auth, session upload, and status polling.
Given a frontend consumer, When reading the spec, Then it clearly understands the required JSON payloads for proxy assignment.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% adherence to OpenAPI 3.0 specification without manual interventions

slices.title: Core Account & Proxy Binding Backend Service
slices.jtbd: When implementing session onboarding for this epic, I want to process OTP codes, parse session files, bind proxies, and enforce daily rate limits, so that the Telegram core integration has valid, isolated sessions to use.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid OTP code, When processed by the backend, Then a new Telegram session is authorized via TDLib.
Given an account reaching its daily limit, When attempting to send a new conversation, Then the action is blocked by the rate limiter.
Given an action dispatch request, When processed, Then the anti-fraud module injects randomized pauses and 'typing' signals.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Reduce session onboarding failure rate to < 1%

slices.title: Account Management UI Dashboard

slices.acceptanceCriteria:

slices.sixSigmaMetric: Sub-100ms UI reactivity for account status updates

slices.title: Inbound Listener and AI Evaluation Backend
